subject: HealCord DPA + model-improvement opt-out — procurement questions
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@healcord.com>
To: k.iyer@redwood.ai <k.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healcord.com
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA questions — no-train + ownership + residency

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Procurement and legal at HealCord are pulling the DPA together and we have a couple of outstanding items where we need a firm commitment from Redwood before we can route this to our CFO for signature: 

1) Explicit no-training / no-model-improvement option: we need contractual language that prevents Redwood from using HealCord production inputs or outputs to improve models (including third-party model training) unless we opt in. Can you confirm the exact wording you can commit to?

2) Prompt & response ownership: HealCord needs an explicit attribution of output IP to the customer for generated content. Does Redwood assign ownership/rights to customers for outputs in all plans?

3) Subprocessor list & residency: we need the current subprocessor list and whether you can route all HealCord traffic to US-only infrastructure (including any cross-border storage for backups). If there are subprocessors outside the US, we need to know which ones and whether onshore-only alternatives exist.

4) Evidence: SOC 2 report plus any attestation that the no-training clause is enforced operationally (logs, KV cache retention policies, audit trail). Procurement would like to see a short evidence pack.

Can you share the DPA redline and subprocessor inventory? Timeline: procurement needs to close the DPA within 10 business days to keep our internal launch dates.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager
HealCord

---
Attachments referenced: procurement-statement_of_needs.pdf (attached by HealCord)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@healcord.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — no-train + ownership + residency

Maya — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front and next steps below.

- No-train / no-model-improvement: Yes — Redwood offers an enforceable "No-Model-Improvement" clause for enterprise DPAs. We can include the following binding language in the amendment: 
  "Redwood will not use Customer Data (including prompts, interactions, and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, adapt, or improve any machine learning models, whether internal or third-party, without Customer's prior written consent."

- Prompt & response ownership: Redwood will grant Customers a perpetual, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, modify, and sublicense outputs generated from their inputs. We include a short IP clause in the amendment to make this explicit.

- Subprocessors & residency: Attached is our current subprocessor inventory and a short matrix showing which subprocessors support onshore routing. We can route HealCord production traffic to US-only regions and keep backups on US-hosted object storage for an additional operational fee or under a Dedicated/Private deployment.

- Evidence: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II report, a redacted audit log sample, and an attestation describing operational controls that prevent training on opted-out traffic (KV cache/retention policy, ingestion gates).

Next steps / ask from HealCord:
  1) Please review the attached DPA amendment (HealCord_DPA_Amendment_v1.pdf) and the subprocessor list.
  2) Confirm whether the no-train opt-out must apply to (a) all accounts under the agreement, or (b) only specified production routes / API keys. We can support either; note that per-route opt-outs are common and operationally feasible.
  3) If residency/onshore routing is required, procurement to confirm whether you want (i) hosted with onshore routing, or (ii) Redwood Dedicated/Private (we'll attach cost delta).

I've looped in Laura (contracts) and Olga (privacy/compliance) for any legal or technical follow-ups. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the amendment.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Contracts (Americas)
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Karthik — quick follow-ups from procurement/legal review: 

1) Scoping the opt-out: HealCord prefers the no-train opt-out to apply to production API keys only (we still want to allow sandbox/test data to be used for model improvement). Can Redwood reflect per-key scoping in the amendment and confirm how that would be operationalized?

2) E2E evidence: procurement needs the SOC 2 and attestation prior to signing. Can you provide the SOC 2 and a one-page attestation document summarizing the operational enforcement (who signs it internally at Redwood)?

3) Cross-border backups: HealCord is US-headquartered but has EU callers for a pilot. For now we require backups and any persisted derivative data to remain in the US. Is the onshore routing option available in your hosted plan or does it require Dedicated?

4) Timeline: can Redwood turn around a redlined amendment (our counsel will redline) and a signed attestation within 5 business days? We need to finalize the DPA next Thursday to meet procurement timelines.

Subject: Re: DPA questions — no-train + ownership + residency

Luca / Maya — good questions. Confirmations and a suggested mutual action plan below.

1) Per-key scoping: We can support per-API-key scoping. Operationally we associate opt-out flags with API keys and exclude flagged traffic from training pipelines and from persistent KV cache snapshots. We'll add the following language to the amendment: 
  "Customer may designate specific API keys or routes as excluded from Machine Learning Model Improvement. Redwood will ensure that traffic associated with excluded keys is segregated and not used to train or improve models."

2) Evidence pack: We'll deliver SOC 2 Type II, the redacted subprocessor list, and a signed one-page attestation (signed by Olga Petrov, Director of Privacy & Compliance) that describes the controls and evidence sources (audit logs, cache retention policy, ingestion gates). Expect these in the next 48 hours.

3) Onshore routing vs Dedicated: Onshore routing for production traffic is available in our hosted offering (we support regional routing and US-only tenancy for enterprise customers). Persistent backups in US-only object storage can be included as part of the DPA amendment for a standard hosting add-on. Dedicated/Private is an alternative if you require tenant isolation or a long-term residency SLA — we'll include both cost profiles in the follow-up.

4) Timeline / next steps: 
  - Aug 19 (end of day): Redwood sends the attestation + SOC 2 link + updated DPA amendment reflecting per-key scoping (action: Redwood).
  - Aug 20: HealCord legal to redline amendment and confirm whether onshore routing add-on is accepted (action: HealCord).
  - Aug 23: Finalize and sign DPA (target).

DocuSign link will be created once both parties confirm the final redline. I've attached the preliminary amendment and the subprocessor list again for convenience. If you want a quick call to run the amendment before redlining, Laura or I can join.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Contracts (Americas)
Redwood Inference
